[caption id="attachment_7314" align="alignleft" width="2560"] From third left: Governor of Lagos State, Mr. Babajide Sanwo-Olu; Head, Marine Waste, Lagos Waste Management Authority (LAWMA) Mr. Lanre Sosore; First Lady of Lagos State, Dr. Mrs. Claudiana Ibijoke Sanwo-Olu; Wife of the Deputy Governor of Lagos State, Her Excellency, Mrs. Oluremi Hamzat (Second right) and Honourable Commissioner for The Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab, during the June edition of the Monthly Environmental Sanitation, held on the 27th of June 2026, at Surulere Local Government, Lagos State.[/caption] [caption id="attachment_7313" align="alignleft" width="1964"] From third left: Governor of Lagos State, Mr. Babajide Sanwo-Olu; Head, Marine Waste, Lagos Waste Management Authority (LAWMA) Mr. Lanre Sosore; First Lady of Lagos State, Dr. Mrs. Claudiana Ibijoke Sanwo-Olu; Wife of the Deputy Governor of Lagos State, Her Excellency, Mrs. Oluremi Hamzat (Second right) and Honourable Commissioner for The Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab, during the June edition of the Monthly Environmental Sanitation, held on the 27th of June 2026, at Surulere Local Government, Lagos State.[/caption]
In his words: "A pick and dump linear waste system cannot be sustainable. Let's even leave climate and others.  We don't even have the land for it. Decades ago, this was at the outskirts; this is an outskirt of Lagos. Today, look around you.  It is an eyesore".
He called on everyone to make waste a resource for wealth, for energy, and all sorts, stressing that, it represents the transition the State is going through now. "You know, for a fact, Larfage is taking our combustible waste to power their machines.  That is out of it. You know that our fruit waste at Ikosi Food Market is working through a bio -digester to power the whole market now. That's also out of the whole chunk generated daily"
"Now, if we take 4,250, and convert to recyclable plastics, our compost fertilizer through Harvest Waste. That takes a substantial part out of it. If we now get Harvest Waste to hit the ground running, they say they want between 1,500 and 2500 tonnes for energy.  That also takes a chunk of it", emphasized. He maintained that in every developed climate of the world, people must start seeing waste as a resource, and that is when the change will be well felt by the citizens. He said in the interim,  the State would get more compactors and also looking at the possibility of EV compactors, which can be integrated into what the PSP operators are doing.
He said the state will bring in tricycle compactors for areas that have grown beyond what PSP operators that were assigned to the original routes can attend to because of narrow lanes and inner roads.
"That will just go to those inner streets. Take them out rather than dumping those things on the streets. or on the median. So that's, that's the long time, but reforms take a while.  It's not a magic wand. But we have to keep fixing what we have on the ground. Remediate why we move towards a bigger picture", he stated.
Prominent among those who accompanied the Commissioner were the Special Adviser on the Environment, Engr Kunle Rotimi-Akodu, Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Dr Gaji Omobolaji Tajudeen,  Managing Director of LAWMA, Dr Muyiwa Gbadegesin, Director, Drainage Construction, Engr Dapo Ajadi who stood in for Permanent Secretary, Drainage Services, Executive Secretary, Lagos State Water Regulatory Commission, Mrs Khadijat Adeyemo and directors.
Meanwhile, Head of Service, Mr. Bode Agoro who led the  monitoring team to Kosofe Local Government expressed satisfaction with the increasing level of residents' participation in the State's monthly environmental sanitation exercise, noting that public response continues to improve as the initiative becomes more established.
Agoro observed that while some residents were yet to fully embrace the sanitation culture, a significant number of people turned out to clean their surroundings.
According to him, "This is the third edition of the exercise, and many residents are beginning to realize that it is not a one-off initiative but a monthly commitment; We are seeing more people coming out to participate, which is encouraging. Although some people were still indoors when the exercise commenced, continued advocacy and public enlightenment will further improve compliance."
He stressed that sustained awareness campaigns remain essential to ensuring greater participation by residents across the State.
He called on all in the Corporate Organization to collaborate with the Government to ensure that the vision of a cleaner environment is collectively achieved.
 "It's a good collaboration where we already have some organisations, like Lafarge on board as part of their Corporate  Social Responsibility on environmental sanitation;  So to all the other corporate organisations emulate people like Lafarge, join us so that we can make the environment cleaner and a better environment," he said.
Agoro reaffirmed the Lagos State Government's commitment to promoting a cleaner, healthier, and more sustainable environment through consistent environmental sanitation exercises and urged residents to continue supporting the initiative by maintaining clean surroundings and complying with environmental regulations.
The Head of Service was accompanied by Chairman Kosofe Local Government Hon. Moyosore Ogunlewe, members of the Body of Permanent Secretaries, Directors in the Ministry as well as Students from Lagos State Education District II.
Signed
Kunle Adeshina
Director, Public Affairs
MOE&WR
June 27, 2026

item.title: LAGOS TO REMOVE ILLEGAL STRUCTURES BLOCKING DRAINAGE CHANNELS ON AGUNGI AND AJIRAN
item.dc:creator: moel
item.content:encoded:
...Warns Developers Against Encroachment on Drainage Right of Way, Insists on Environmental Compliance.
The Lagos State Government has declared that it will immediately remove all illegal structures obstructing canals and drainage channel right of way along Agungi, Ajiran and Ikota areas of the State.
The State reaffirmed its commitment to eliminating perennial flooding across Lagos, regardless of the status of developers or individuals responsible for the encroachments.
The Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab, made this known after an extensive inspection tour of critical drainage infrastructure and flood mitigation projects in Lekki, Agungi, Ikota and Ajiran.
The inspection followed persistent reports of flooding in Agungi despite the completion of major drainage infrastructure in the area over two years ago.
Speaking during the tour, the Commissioner disclosed that the inspection uncovered a major obstruction responsible for the recurring flooding at Ajiran, where a land-owning family was discovered to have blocked the Ajiran outfall channel.
According to him, the family had illegally obstructed the outlet of a primary drainage channel leading directly into the Lagos Lagoon, preventing stormwater from flowing freely out of the community.
[caption id="attachment_7322" align="alignleft" width="2400"] L-R: Managing Director, Lagos Waste Management Authority (LAWMA) Dr. Muyiwa Gbadegesin; Executive Secretary, Water Regulatory, Mrs. Adebukola Adeyemo; Honourable Commissioner for The Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab; Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Dr. Gaji Omobolaji and Permanent Secretary, Office of Drainage Services, Engr. Mahamood Adegbite, during a drainage tour on the 28th of June, 2026 at Chevron drive, Lekki, Lagos State.[/caption] [caption id="attachment_7321" align="alignleft" width="2400"] L-R: Special Adviser on Environment, Engr. Olakunle Rotimi-Akodu; Honourable Commissioner for The Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab; Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Dr. Gaji Omobolaji; Managing Directory (Akf) properties limited, Mr. Ayodeji Fadoju and Permanent Secretary, Office of Drainage Services, Engr. Mahamood Adegbite, during a drainage tour on 28th of June, 2026 to Megamound Estate, Ikota, Lagos State.[/caption] [caption id="attachment_7320" align="alignleft" width="2312"] L-R: Managing Director, Lagos Waste Management Authority (LAWMA) Dr. Muyiwa Gbadegesin; Executive Secretary, Water Regulatory, Mrs. Adebukola Adeyemo; Honourable Commissioner for The Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab; Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Dr. Gaji Omobolaji and Permanent Secretary, Office of Drainage Services, Engr. Mahamood Adegbite, during a drainage tour on the 28th of June, 2026 at Chevron drive, Lekki, Lagos State.[/caption]
He explained that the drainage infrastructure was specifically designed to discharge floodwater by gravity into the lagoon, stressing that blocking the outlet had significantly impaired the effectiveness of the system.
"We discovered that the outlet into the lagoon had been deliberately blocked; Without opening that channel, the water cannot leave the area. We have therefore directed that it be reopened immediately in the overriding public interest," he said.
Wahab emphasized that while the Government recognizes legitimate land ownership and respects Certificates of Occupancy, no individual or family has the right to obstruct natural watercourses or public drainage infrastructure.
"No one is above the law; having title to land does not give anyone the authority to close a drainage channel or water body that serves thousands of residents; We are not taking anyone's land; we are simply restoring the channel to allow water flow into the lagoon," he stated.
The Commissioner noted that the flooding situation in Agungi and Ajiran is unique because the communities depend on a dedicated drainage channel that conveys stormwater through Chevron Drive into the Lagos Lagoon.
He warned that when drainage channels are blocked, residents ultimately bear the consequences through severe flooding, despite significant public investment in drainage infrastructure.
"You can imagine the level of flooding within the community, and eventually government gets blamed for inadequate infrastructure; Taxpayers' money is being used to construct and maintain these drainage channels; Residents should not make the situation worse by blocking them;  We will continue to open up blocked drainage channels wherever they are found in the overriding public interest," he said.
During the inspection, the Commissioner also visited Megamond Estate in Ikota, where developers were found to have illegally reclaimed part of the Ikota River and commenced construction without obtaining the necessary environmental and drainage approvals adding that some developments had extended beyond the approvals granted by the State Government.
He disclosed that enforcement and abatement notices had previously been served  to the developers but were ignored.
"From tomorrow morning, all illegal structures erected on reclaimed drainage alignments without approval in this estate will be removed; This action will sends a clear message that Lagos  will not tolerate encroachment on drainage channels or public infrastructures.
Wahab clarified that investigations confirmed that no application or approval had ever been granted for the development in question at at Ikota, adding that enforcement would proceed without delay.
The Commissioner also reiterated that all developments involving wetlands or water-related projects must comply strictly with environmental regulations before construction begins.
According to him, developers are required to obtain an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) and, where applicable, Wetland Clearance from the Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources before commencing any reclamation or construction activities.
He explained that the Environmental Impact Assessment is a fundamental requirement because it evaluates the potential effects of a proposed development on the surrounding ecosystem and determines appropriate mitigation measures.
Wahab added that the Ministry operates an integrated approval process, with close collaboration between the Office of Drainage Services and other relevant departments to ensure that drainage, environmental and wetland considerations are addressed before any approval is granted.
He lamented that many developers deliberately bypass these statutory requirements by commencing reclamation and construction without approvals, hoping to seek regularisation afterwards.
He stressed that the Government would continue removing all illegal reclamations and developments that violate environmental laws.
"We don't care whose ox is gored. It is unfair to the system, unfair to law-abiding residents and unacceptable because it compromises public safety."
He also appealed to residents to remain vigilant and continue supporting the Government by reporting environmental infractions.
"We encourage Lagosians to see something and say something. The illegal activities discovered during today's inspection came to our attention through whistleblowers. We investigated, verified the reports and acted immediately. Residents have a critical role to play in protecting our drainage infrastructure."
Wahab assured residents that the Lagos State Government remains fully committed to safeguarding lives, property and public infrastructure through strict enforcement of environmental laws and continuous investment in resilient drainage infrastructure.
The Commissioner was accompanied by the Special Adviser on Environment Mr Olakunle Rotimi-Akodu, Permanent Secretary Office of Environmental Services, Gaji Omobolaji, Permanent Secretary Office of Drainage Services Engr Mahamood Adegbite.
Other are the Managing Director LAWMA, Dr Muyiwa Gbadegesin, Executive Secretary, LASWARCO, Mrs Adebukola Adeyemo, KAI Marshal, Major Olatunbosun Cole as well as Directors in the Ministry.

Director Public Affairs

item.title: LAGOS SUES FOR CALM FOLLOWING 2 WEEKS PERSISTENT RAINFALLS & FLASH FLOODS AS SANWO-OLU APPROVES IMMEDIATE DREDGING MAINTENANCE OF 28 ADDITIONAL PRIMARY CHANNELS
item.dc:creator: moel
item.content:encoded:
The Lagos State Government on Tuesday called for calm and understanding from residents following the massive flash flooding experienced in many parts of the State over the last two weeks, with the Governor, Mr Babajide Sanwo-Olu, approving the immediate dredging and maintenance of 28 additional primary channels across the state.
Speaking against the backdrop of the heavy downpours which caused flash flooding in many communities, the Honourable Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab, said the rainfalls were an extreme weather event that produced an unusually high volume of water within a short period, overwhelming drainage channels in some locations and resulting in temporary flooding across parts of Victoria Island, Lekki, Ikeja, Gbagada, Mushin, Mafoluku and several other areas.
According to the Commissioner, the incident was not peculiar to Lagos, as a similar heavy rainfalls also affected other African Countries on the same day, even in North America resulting in flooding across some cities noting that while Lagos and these cities have coastal and hydraulic characteristics, Lagos presents a much more complex hydrological system due to its extensive network of lagoons, tidal water bodies, rivers and creeks, as well as significantly higher rainfall intensity.
He explained that the interaction between the Atlantic Ocean, Lagos Lagoon and numerous rivers and creeks, particularly during periods of high tide, naturally slows the discharge of stormwater into the sea, resulting in temporary inundation in some low-lying areas whenever exceptionally heavy rainfall occurs.
Wahab assured residents that the Lagos State Government remains fully on top of the situation through continuous monitoring of drainage infrastructure, flood-prone locations and other critical water channels, adding that emergency response agencies have remained on the ground to ensure that floodwaters recede as quickly as weather conditions permit while providing support where necessary.
The Commissioner stressed that while the State Government continues to invest significantly in drainage construction, channelisation, desilting and other flood control infrastructure, residents also have an important role to play in reducing the impact of flooding.
He urged residents to desist from indiscriminate disposal of refuse into drains, canals and waterways, illegal reclamation of wetlands, construction on drainage alignments and other activities that obstruct the free flow of stormwater, noting that such actions worsen flooding during periods of intense rainfall.
Wahab stated that the effects of climate change are becoming increasingly evident across the world, with coastal cities experiencing more frequent and intense rainfall events.
"Lagos is not exempted from these realities; However, the State Government remains steadfast in its commitment to building a flood-resilient city through sustained infrastructure development, environmental enforcement and active collaboration with residents," he said.
He reiterated that protecting Lagos from the impacts of flooding is a shared responsibility and called on all residents to support government efforts by keeping drainage channels free of waste and reporting any activity capable of obstructing the free flow of stormwater.
He also advised motorists to avoid driving through flooded roads during heavy downpours and appealed to residents, particularly those in flood-prone areas, to heed weather advisories and comply with safety instructions issued by relevant government agencies and which the ministry issues on a daily basis.
He thereafter reaffirmed the Lagos State Government's commitment to safeguarding lives and property through proactive flood management measures while urging residents to continue to cooperate with government in building a cleaner, safer and more resilient Lagos.
Signed
Kunle Adeshina
Director Public Affairs
MOE&WR
30th June, 2026

item.title: WE WILL SUSTAIN CLEARANCE OF ILLEGAL OCCUPANTS ON OKOKOMAIKO –ORILE ROAD MEDIAN, ENFORCE ENVIRONMENTAL LAWS -LASG
item.dc:creator: moel
item.content:encoded:
The Lagos State Government on Wednesday reaffirmed its determination to permanently rid the Okokomaiko–Orile road median of illegal traders and squatters, declaring that the encroached median has been designated for the Lagos Rail Mass Transit project and must remain free for its intended purpose.
The Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab, made the declaration during an inspection of the ongoing dislodgement exercise being carried out in compliance with the directive of the Governor of Lagos State to clear all illegal structures and commercial activities obstructing the road median along the busy highway.
Speaking during the inspection, Wahab said the visit was to assess the level of compliance and evaluate the progress of the exercise, noting that the State Government had consistently engaged the traders over the years without lasting success.
He stated that the continued occupation of the median by traders could no longer be tolerated, describing the development as an abuse of critical public infrastructure constructed with taxpayers' money.
[caption id="attachment_7328" align="alignleft" width="2011"] L-R: Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Dr. Gaji Omobolaji; Honourable Commissioner for The Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab; Chairman, Lagos State Taskforce, CSP. Adebayo Akerele; Special Adviser on Environment, Engr. Olakunle Rotimi-Akodu and Permanent Secretary, Office of Drainage Services, Engr. Mahamood Adegbite, during an inspector tour on the 1st of July, 2026 to the ongoing clean up at Lagos Badagry express way, Lagos State.[/caption]
[caption id="attachment_7329" align="alignleft" width="2211"] L-R: Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Dr. Gaji Omobolaji; Honourable Commissioner for The Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab; Special Adviser on Environment, Engr. Olakunle Rotimi-Akodu; Managing Director, Lagos Waste Management Authority (LAWMA), Dr. Muyiwa Gbadegesin and Permanent Secretary, Office of Drainage Services, Engr. Mahamood Adegbite, during an inspector tour on the 1st of July, 2026 to the ongoing clean up at Lagos Badagry express way, Lagos State.[/caption]
According to him, "This is a major highway built with public funds. For years, we have repeatedly engaged those occupying the median and consistently pushed them back from the Okokomaiko end to Orile; Enough is enough. We are determined to permanently clear this corridor and ensure that it remains free from all forms of encroachment."
The Commissioner explained that the wide road median was deliberately designed to accommodate the Lagos Rail Mass Transit project and warned that the State Government would sustain regular monitoring and enforcement to prevent a return of illegal occupants.
"We will continue to patrol this stretch and ensure that those dislodged do not return; This median has been reserved for the rail project, and it must be protected for that purpose," he added.
Addressing environmental sanitation, Wahab urged residents to adopt responsible waste disposal practices by patronising their assigned Private Sector Participation (PSP) waste operators, stressing that indiscriminate dumping of refuse on roads, medians and other public spaces remains unacceptable.
He encouraged residents to report any failure in waste collection by PSP operators to the Lagos Waste Management Authority (LAWMA), assuring them that service providers are obligated to render efficient services.
"It does not reflect positively on us as a people when waste generated in our homes is dumped on road medians and other public places. Residents should patronise their PSP operators and immediately report any failure in service delivery to LAWMA. There is no justification for indiscriminate waste disposal," he said.
The Commissioner also disclosed that the State Government was intensifying sanitation enforcement across markets, warning that market leaders and traders must take responsibility for maintaining clean trading environments.
"If traders cannot keep their markets clean, then they should not be doing business there. Environmental cleanliness is a collective responsibility and must be taken seriously by everyone," he said.
Wahab revealed that the Ministry has, within the last one year, prosecuted more than 100 offenders for encroaching on road medians and violating environmental regulations.
He maintained that Lagos State environmental laws provide clear sanctions for acts that undermine public infrastructure and environmental sustainability, stressing that enforcement would continue without fear or favour.
The Commissioner reiterated the commitment of the Lagos State Government to protecting critical public infrastructure, preserving the alignment for the Lagos Rail Mass Transit project, improving environmental sanitation and ensuring that Lagos remains a clean, resilient and sustainable city for all.
The Commissioner was accompanied by the Special Adviser on Environment Engr. Olakunle Rotimi-Akodu, Permanent Secretary Office of Environmental Services Gaji Omobolaji, Permanent Secretary,  Office of Drainage Services Engr Mahamood Adegbite, Lagos State Taskforce Chairman, CSP  Adebayo Akerele, Managing Director LAWMA Dr Muyiwa Gbadegesin as well as Directors from the Ministry.
Signed
Kunle Adeshina,
 Director
Public Affairs
 MOE&WR,
1st July, 2026

item.title: LAGOS INTENSIFIES DRAINAGE RESTORATION, ENFORCEMENT AGAINST ENCROACHMENT TO PREVENT FLOODING.
item.dc:creator: moel
item.content:encoded:
The Lagos State Government has reiterated its commitment to restoring and protecting critical drainage infrastructure across the State as part of sustained efforts to mitigate flooding, preserve the environment and safeguard lives and property.
The Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab, gave the assurance on Saturday during an inspection tour of ongoing contravention removal and drainage restoration works in the Ajiran/Agungi axis of the Eti-Osa Local Government Area.
Speaking with the  media after the inspection, Wahab recalled that the State Government had recently uncovered extensive encroachment on the primary drainage channel in Chevron Drive by individuals and land-owning families who illegally took possession of government setbacks, thereby obstructing the free flow of stormwater.
He disclosed that despite an attempt by some individuals, aided by armed policemen, to frustrate government officials from carrying out lawful exercise of reopening the Ajiran Channel to the Lagoon and the Ikota River, the State remained resolute and successfully continued the operation.
According to him, the intervention has already yielded positive results, with a remarkable improvement in stormwater discharge within 48 to 72 hours, bringing relief to residents of Agungi, Ajiran Village and neighbouring communities.
The Commissioner explained that the visit was to assess the level of progress made, stressing that the exercise remains a work in progress until the entire drainage alignment is fully restored and reconnected to the natural water bodies.
During the visit the Commissioner also met with community leaders and residents in Ajiran to explain the ongoing intervention, answer questions and provide detailed information on both immediate and long-term measures being implemented to permanently address flooding in the area.
Wahab said the Ministry is collaborating with the Ministry of Works and Infrastructure to deliver a sustainable engineering solution for the flood-prone corridor.
Wahab also directed the Emergency Flood Abatement Gang (EFAG) to immediately commence remedial maintenance works on some drainage channels requiring urgent intervention in the area, noting that government cannot delay action where public safety is concerned.
[caption id="attachment_7337" align="alignleft" width="2400"] L-R: Honourable Commissioner for The Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab; Special Adviser on Environment, Engr. Olakunle Rotimi-Akodu; Permanent Secretary, Office of Drainage Services, Engr. Mahamood Adegbite and Drainage Maintenance Coordinator, Eti Osa, Engr. Yetunde Okanlawon, during a drainage tour on the 4th of July, 2026 to Iru, Eti-Osa, Victoria Island, Lagos State.[/caption] [caption id="attachment_7336" align="alignleft" width="1536"] L-R: A resident of Agungi, Mr. Eyimisan Abusomwan; Special Adviser on Environment, Engr. Olakunle Rotimi-Akodu; Honourable Commissioner for The Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab; Director Drainage Construction, Office of Drainage Services, Engr. Dapo Ajadi and Permanent Secretary, Office of Drainage Services, Engr. Mahamood Adegbite, during a drainage tour on 4th of July, 2026 to Agungi, Lekki, Lagos State.[/caption]
The team also visited Orange Island on Freedom Way, where the Commissioner reaffirmed government's resolve against illegal dredging and land reclamation.
He recalled that the Ministry had halted reclamation activities at the location last year because the developers failed to obtain the mandatory Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) approval and drainage clearance.
According to him, the area serves as a major discharge outlet for Lekki Phase I into the Lagoon, warning that any obstruction through illegal reclamation would create significant environmental challenges and heighten flood risks.
Wahab also inspected the downstream discharge points serving Itedo, Kushenla and Freedom Way, where additional corrective measures have been identified for immediate implementation.
While commending the efforts of the Local Government authorities in improving their operational capacity, he emphasised that flood management requires collaboration among all tiers of government and residents.
He noted that while the State Government will continue to provide major drainage infrastructure, Local Government and communities must take ownership of completed facilities by ensuring regular maintenance and preventing indiscriminate dumping of refuse into drainage channels.
The Commissioner explained that every newly constructed road must be accompanied by properly designed collector drains connected to primary canals to guarantee efficient stormwater discharge.
Speaking on the State's environmental reforms, Wahab said the government has, over the last three years, implemented deliberate policies aimed at addressing the root causes of flooding and environmental degradation.
He listed the reforms to include improved waste collection systems, the ban on styrofoam food containers, removal of illegal structures on flood plains, protection of wetlands and continuous investment in resilient drainage infrastructure.
Drawing comparisons with recent flooding incidents in Ghana, the Commissioner noted that many of the measures now being considered by authorities in Accra are policies Lagos has consistently implemented over the past three years.
He maintained that Lagos is not experiencing river overflow but rather temporary flash floods during periods of intense rainfall, explaining that floodwaters usually recede within hours once drainage channels remain free of obstruction.
Addressing concerns over indiscriminate waste disposal, Wahab disclosed that the State Government has continued to arrest and prosecute environmental offenders while intensifying public enlightenment campaigns to discourage illegal dumping of refuse stressing that enforcement alone would not solve the problem.
The Commissioner announced that the State Government will soon deploy between 140 and 150 additional waste compactors to strengthen LAWMA's fleet while also supporting PSP operators to improve waste evacuation across Lagos.
He further revealed that Lagos is accelerating its transition from a linear waste management system to a circular economy where waste is treated as a valuable resource.
According to him, the commencement of Material Recovery Facilities and Transfer Loading Stations before the end of the year is expected to divert over 4,000 tonnes of waste daily from landfills, significantly improving waste management efficiency and environmental sustainability across the State.
Wahab reiterated that the Lagos State Government will remain unwavering in enforcing environmental laws, protecting drainage alignments and delivering sustainable infrastructure necessary to build a flood-resilient and cleaner Lagos.
Signed
Kunle Adeshina
Director
Public Affairs
MOE&WR
4th July 2026

item.title: LASG SIGNS MOU WITH CHINA HARBOUR AND NASTON ENGINEERING TO ADVANCE WATER INFRASTRUCTURE DEVELOPMENT.
item.dc:creator: moel
item.content:encoded:
The Lagos State Government on Thursday signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with China Harbour Engineering Company (CHEC) and Naston Engineering Nigeria Limited to commence the scoping and definition of key components of the State's water infrastructure development aimed at expanding access to potable water across Lagos.
Speaking at the signing ceremony, the Honourable Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab, described the agreement as a major step towards strengthening the State's water supply infrastructure and reaffirmed the commitment of the Lagos State Government to providing sustainable, safe and reliable potable water for its growing population.
The Commissioner noted that the one-year MoU provides a collaborative framework for the development of two strategic project lots that will form the foundation for the next phase of water infrastructure expansion in the State.
"Under the agreement, the first project lot will focus on the installation of a water transmission pipeline beneath the Lagos Lagoon into the Lekki Concession Area"
"While the second project lot will define downstream distribution activities including metering and last-mile connections within the concession area" he said
Wahab said at the end of the engagement, the State is expected to receive a comprehensive technical report and implementation framework that will guide the execution of the projects and facilitate the preparation of a concession agreement between the Lagos State Government and the consortium.
[caption id="attachment_7342" align="alignleft" width="2400"] L-R: Executive Director, China Harbour Engineering Company, Lagos State, Luke Lin; Executive Director, Naston Engineering Nigeria, Mrs. Remi Agbowu; Managing Director, Naston Engineering Ltd, Mr. Kole Funsho; Honourable Commissioner, Ministry of The Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab; Permanent Secretary, Office of Drainage Services, Engr. Mahamood Adegbite; Managing Director, Lagos Water Corporation, Engr. Mukhtaar Tijani and Executive Director operations, Lagos Water Corporation, Engr. Lanke Taiwo, during the signing of (MoU) between Lagos State Government and China Harbour and Naston Engineering, on the 9th of July, 2026, at Alausa Secretariat, Lagos State.[/caption]
Speaking on behalf of Naston Engineering Nigeria Limited, the  Managing Director, Mr. Kole Funsho, expressed appreciation to the Lagos State Government for the confidence reposed in the consortium, describing the signing of the MoU as the beginning of a process that would culminate in the delivery of a robust and bankable water infrastructure project.
He explained that the agreement clearly defines the scope of the proposed concession and affirmed the consortium's commitment to delivering the required technical studies within the stipulated timeframe, or even ahead of schedule.
He disclosed that the consortium would prepare detailed engineering designs, project cost estimates and tariff structures required to support the final concession agreement with the Lagos State Government.
According to him, the successful execution of the assignment will require close collaboration with the Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources as well as other relevant government agencies to obtain critical drainage and infrastructure data needed to properly align the proposed transmission pipelines without disrupting existing roads, drainage systems and other public infrastructure.
He expressed optimism that the partnership between the consortium and the Lagos State Government would pave the way for the successful implementation of the projects and significantly improve potable water supply to residents of the State.
Also present at the signing ceremony was the Permanent Secretary Office of Drainage Services Engr Mahamood Adegbite, Managing Director, Lagos Wayer Corporation, Engr Mukhtaar Tijani, Executive Director Operation, LWC, as well as  China Harbour Engineering Company Executive Director, Mr. Luke Lin, alongside members of its executive management team.
Signed
Kunle Adeshina
Director
Public Affairs
MOE&WR,
9th July, 2026.

item.title: SANWO-OLU RALLIES LAGOSIANS TO PLANT, NURTURE TREES FOR A GREENER, MORE RESILIENT LAGOS
item.dc:creator: moel
item.content:encoded:
... State Targets 20,000 Trees to Boost Climate Resilience as it Celebrates 2026 Tree Planting Day

Lagos State Governor, Mr. Babajide Olusola Sanwo-Olu, has called on all Lagosians to actively participate in tree planting and, more importantly, nurture every tree planted as part of the collective effort to build a greener, healthier and more climate-resilient State.
Speaking at the 2026 Tree Planting Day celebration held at Eko Amore Gardens, Freedom Way, Lekki on Tuesday, the Governor described the annual event as a demonstration of the State's commitment to environmental sustainability and climate action through nature-based solutions.
The Governor, represented by the Secretary to the State Government, Barr. Abimbola Salu- Hundeyin stressed that planting trees alone is not enough, noting that their true value lies in ensuring they survive and mature.
He commended the Lagos State Parks and Gardens Agency (LASPARK) for its commitment to greening the State, saying the agency's efforts continue to strengthen Lagos' resilience against the impacts of climate change, including rising temperatures and flooding.
The Governor noted that trees help cool the environment, improve air quality, reduce flood risks and enhance public health, adding that environmental stewardship is a shared responsibility that requires the participation of government, communities, schools, traditional institutions, corporate organisations and residents.
[caption id="attachment_7347" align="alignleft" width="2400"] L-R: Permanent Secretary, Office of Drainage Services, Engr. Mahamood Adegbite; Chairman, Agege Local Government, Hon. Vinod Obasa; Honourable Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab; Representative of the Governor of Lagos State and Secretary to the State Government, Barr. Abimbola Salu-Hundeyin; Wife of the Deputy Governor of Lagos State, Mrs. Oluremi Hamzat and General Manager, Lagos State Parks and Gardens Agency, Mrs. Adetoun Popoola, during the year 2026 annual tree planting exercise, held on the 14th of July, 2026, at the Eko Amore Gardens, Freedom way, Lagos State.[/caption] [caption id="attachment_7345" align="alignleft" width="2400"] L-R: Permanent Secretary, Office of Drainage Services, Engr. Mahamood Adegbite; Chairman, Agege Local Government, Hon. Vinod Obasa; Honourable Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab; Representative of the Governor of Lagos State and Secretary to the State Government, Barr. Abimbola Salu-Hundeyin; Wife of the Deputy Governor of Lagos State, Mrs. Oluremi Hamzat and General Manager, Lagos State Parks and Gardens Agency, Mrs. Adetoun Popoola, during the year 2026 annual tree planting exercise, held on the 14th of July, 2026, at the Eko Amore Gardens, Freedom way, Lagos State.[/caption]
Providing an update on the State's tree planting campaign, Sanwo-Olu disclosed that 13,401 trees—representing 67 per cent of the State's 20,000-tree target—had been planted across the five divisions of Lagos as of June 30, 2026, with all trees being monitored by LASPARK to ensure their survival.
He announced the commencement of a new planting season across all 57 Local Government Areas and Local Council Development Areas, which will run throughout the rainy season until October to exceed the annual target.
The Governor charged the Chairmen of the 57 LGAs and LCDAs to serve as "Tree Custodians" by working closely with LASPARK to protect and monitor trees within their communities, while reminding residents that anyone who unlawfully fells a tree must replace it with five others in accordance with State law.
As part of this year's celebration, Governor Sanwo-Olu also unveiled the 20 Lagos Tree Champions, recognising individuals and organisations whose outstanding contributions have advanced the greening of Lagos.
He noted that the initiative aligns with the Environment and Health pillar of the THEMES+ Development Agenda while urging residents to obtain free tree seedlings from LASPARK's nurseries in Ikorodu and Agege for planting in homes, schools, offices and communities.
"We are not just planting trees; we are planting hope and a lasting legacy. Together, we can build a Lagos that is cooler, cleaner, safer, flood-resilient and more beautiful for future generations," the Governor said.
In his welcome address, the Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab, described the annual exercise as a strategic environmental intervention aimed at combating the growing effects of climate change while encouraging environmental stewardship among residents.
Wahab highlighted the theme for the 2026 celebration, "Trees for Lagos: Our City, Our Responsibility."
said the celebration goes beyond a ceremonial event, noting that it serves as a reminder that protecting the environment is a shared responsibility.
He observed that the increasing occurrence of extreme weather events, flooding, land degradation, biodiversity loss and rising temperatures across the globe underscores the urgent need for collective climate action, adding that tree planting remains one of the simplest and most effective nature-based solutions to mitigate these environmental challenges.
According to him, trees play a critical role in improving air quality, absorbing carbon dioxide, conserving water, enriching the soil, reducing flooding and erosion, providing habitats for wildlife and enhancing the overall health and wellbeing of communities, while also supporting economic activities such as agriculture, forestry and tourism.
Wahab further announced that all Local Government Areas and Local Council Development Areas have been designated as Tree Custodians, with the responsibility of nurturing and monitoring the trees planted within their jurisdictions for a minimum period of 12 months to ensure sustainability and improve survival rates.
He urged residents to see every tree planted as an investment in the future, calling on all Lagosians to nurture the trees and embrace environmentally responsible practices that will safeguard the State's natural heritage for generations to come.
Wahab also encouraged residents to plant not only trees but also the values of hope, unity, responsibility and environmental consciousness, expressing confidence that through collective action, Lagos will continue to set the pace in sustainable environmental management in Nigeria.
In her goodwill message, the wife of the Deputy Governor, Mrs Oluremi Hamzat said the future of the environment depends on the choices residents make and engage in.
Hamzat said Lagos is one of  Africa's fastest-growing cities continues to face the challenges of rapid urbanisation, rising temperatures, flooding and environmental degradation.
She maintained that  planting and nurturing trees remains one of the simplest yet most effective ways to improve air quality, reduce heat, preserve biodiversity and build healthier, more resilient communities.
She stressed that Tree planting is more than an environmental exercise but an investment in the health, safety and prosperity of future generations.
She encouraged every Lagosian, families, schools, faith-based organisations, market associations and the private sector—to make tree planting a way of life. saying that it must become a lasting legacy for generations to come.
A total of 21 Tree Champions drawn from the real estate sector, schools, private sector, amongst others, were presented with awards to recognise and appreciate their contributions and commitment to the Lagos Greening Initiative.
The highpoint of the event was the ceremonial planting of Trees by every dignitary at the event, which included the Governor, Wife of the Deputy Governor, Mrs Oluremi Hamzat, Chairman, Agege Local Government, Hon Vinod Obasa, Permanent Secretary, Office of Drainage Services, amongst others.
Kunle Adeshina,
Director, Public Affairs,
MOE&WR,
14 July, 2026.

item.title: LAGOS INTENSIFIES GRASSROOTS ENVIRONMENTAL ADVOCACY, URGES RESIDENTS TO EMBRACE RESPONSIBLE WASTE DISPOSAL
item.dc:creator: moel
item.content:encoded:
The Lagos State Government has reaffirmed that achieving a cleaner, healthier and flood-resilient environment requires the active participation of all residents, stressing that environmental sustainability can only be attained through collective responsibility and lasting behavioural change.

Speaking at a Stakeholders' Environmental Enlightenment Campaign held at the Amuwo Odofin Local Government Secretariat on Friday, the Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Dr. Gaji Omobolaji, said the campaign forms part of the State Government's ongoing efforts to strengthen public awareness and promote responsible waste management practices across communities.

Represented by the Director of the Environmental Assessment Department, Dr. Olasunkanmi Sojinu, the Permanent Secretary explained that the initiative supports the vision of Governor Babajide Olusola Sanwo-Olu to build a cleaner, healthier, safer and more sustainable Lagos through inclusive stakeholder engagement and continuous environmental advocacy.

[caption id="attachment_7354" align="alignleft" width="1280"] L-R: Representative of the Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services and Director, Environmental Impact Assessment, Office of Environmental Services, Dr. Olasunkanmi Sojinu; Chairman, Amuwo Odofin LGA, Prince Lanre Sanusi; Director, Environmental Monitoring Unit, Office of Environmental Services, Mrs. Omoyeni Balogun and the Supervisor on Environment, Amuwo Odofin LGA. Hon. Ibrahim Balogun, during a Stakeholders Enlightenment programme, held on 17th of July, 2026, at Amuwo Odofin LGA, Lagos State.[/caption] [caption id="attachment_7352" align="alignleft" width="1448"] L-R: Representative of the Permanent Secretary, Office of Urban Development, TPL. Alaka Olufemi; Representative of the Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services and Director Environmental Impact Assessment, Office of Environmental Services, Dr. Olasunkanmi Sojinu; Chairman, Amuwo Odofin LGA, Prince. Lanre Sanusi; Director Environmental Monitoring Unit, Office of Environmental Services, Mrs. Omoyeni Balogun and the Surpervisor on Environment, Amuwo Odofin LGA. Hon. Ibrahim Balogun, during a Stakeholders Enlightenment programme, held on 17th of July, 2026, at Amuwo Odofin LGA, Lagos State.[/caption]

He noted that Lagos, as Nigeria's commercial hub and one of Africa's fastest-growing megacities, generates enormous volumes of waste daily. While the State Government has continued to invest heavily in waste management infrastructure, drainage maintenance, recycling programmes, environmental sanitation and public enlightenment, he emphasised that the success of these initiatives depends largely on residents adopting responsible waste disposal habits.

Dr. Gaji identified indiscriminate waste disposal as one of the State's greatest environmental challenges, noting that refuse is still being dumped on roads, medians, drainage channels and other unauthorised locations. According to him, such practices obstruct drainage systems, contribute to flooding, degrade the environment, threaten public health and undermine government investments in environmental management.

He stressed that environmental cleanliness is a shared responsibility. While government will continue to provide infrastructure, formulate policies and enforce environmental laws, he said residents, businesses, market leaders, transport operators, religious organisations and community associations all have vital roles to play in maintaining a clean environment.

The Permanent Secretary reiterated the State Government's commitment to promoting voluntary compliance through sustained public education, dialogue and community partnerships, noting that behavioural change remains more effective and sustainable than enforcement alone.

"We would rather educate than prosecute, prevent than penalise, and build a culture of environmental responsibility across our communities," he said.

He disclosed that government has intensified environmental monitoring, routine sanitation inspections, drainage maintenance, evacuation of waste from illegal dumpsites and enforcement against environmental offenders. Surveillance has also been strengthened across highways, markets, transport corridors and identified environmental hotspots to discourage indiscriminate waste disposal.

Dr. Gaji called on Local Governments and Local Council Development Areas (LCDAs) to sustain environmental awareness campaigns at the grassroots by mobilising residents and strengthening community participation. He also urged traditional institutions, Community Development Associations (CDAs), market associations, transport unions, the media and the private sector to continue championing responsible environmental practices within their respective communities.

He further advised residents to patronise only approved Private Sector Participation (PSP) waste operators, dispose of waste responsibly, keep drainage channels free of refuse and promptly report environmental violations through the appropriate government channels.

According to him, the environmental objectives of the State Government's THEMES+ Development Agenda can only be achieved when every resident recognises that environmental responsibility begins with individual actions.

The Permanent Secretary encouraged participants to become ambassadors of environmental responsibility by promoting proper sanitation and effective waste management practices within their homes, workplaces and communities. He expressed confidence that sustained collaboration, shared responsibility and continuous public enlightenment would enable Lagos to make significant progress towards becoming a cleaner, healthier and more environmentally sustainable city for both present and future generations.

In his welcome address, the Chairman of Amuwo Odofin Local Government, Prince Lanre Sanusi, said a clean environment attracts investment, improves economic productivity and enhances the overall quality of life. He described environmental sustainability as a shared responsibility of the State Government, Local Government and residents, urging participants to embrace proper waste management practices and become advocates of environmental responsibility wherever they live and work.

The stakeholders' enlightenment campaign was attended by community leaders, traditional rulers, market associations, transport unions, environmental stakeholders and residents from across the local government area.

item.title: SANWO -OLU WIFE URGES RESIDENTS TO MAKE CLEANINESS OF THE ENVIRONMENT, A DAILY AFFAIR
item.dc:creator: moel
item.content:encoded:
...Exercise Monitored in Ibeju-Lekki by Deputy Governor's Wife, Environment Commissioner; SA Environment Leads Badagry Team
The First Lady of Lagos State, Dr Claudiana Ibijoke-Sanwo-Olu, on Saturday urged all residents not to wait till the last Saturday of the month to embark on the cleaning of their environment but make it an everyday affair.
The First Lady spoke at Eputu 'London' in Ibeju- Lekki Local Government when she monitored the July edition of the sanitation exercise alongside the wife of the Deputy Governor, Mrs Oluremi Hamzat, and Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Mr Tokunbo Wahab, and selected Permanent Secretaries and top officials of the State.
Dr Sanwo-Olu expressed appreciation to the residents of Eputu 'London' who came out in their large numbers to participate in the exercise,saying: "We are very, very proud of our people. We noticed today that in Ebutu London, both the children and the parents came out very early to clean their environment"
"Even though we are noticing that we have all the floods and things happening in Lagos State, we are making a conscious effort to create awareness among our people to ensure that they remove all the debris as much as possible", she stated.
While describing the participation of people as a work in progress, the First Lady said that explains why school pupils are being involved so that the message of cleanliness can be imbibed at a younger age.
She added that this would ensure that whatever is handed down over to them, they will continue with it as they grow into adulthood.
Dr Sanwo-Olu gave a commitment that from the August edition, students of tertiary institutions will also form a part of the monitoring of the monthly sanitation exercise.
[caption id="attachment_7361" align="alignleft" width="2170"] L-R: Honourable Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab; Olori Ogunfolu Kingdom, Ibeju-Lekki, Her Royal Majesty, Afolashade Ojuolape Idogun; Chairman, Ibeju-Lekki Local Government, Hon. Sesan Olowa ; Ologunfayo of Ogunfolu Kingdom, Ibeju-Lekki, His Royal Majesty, Oba. Dr. Mufutau Olanrewaju Idogun (Tunwase 1); First Lady Dr (Mrs) Claudiana Ibijoke Sanwo-Olu and Wife of the Deputy Governor of Lagos State, Mrs. Oluremi Hamzat, during the Monthly Environmental Sanitation Exercise, held on the 25th of July, 2026, at Ibeju-Lekki Local Government, Lagos State[/caption] [caption id="attachment_7360" align="alignleft" width="1980"] From Second left; Honourable Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab; Olori of Ogunfayo Kingdom, Ibeju-Lekki, Olori Afolashde Ojuolape Idogun; Ologunfayo of Ogunfayo Kingdom, Ibeju-Lekki, HRM, Oba. Dr. Mufutau Olanrewaju Idogun (Tunwase 1); First Lady, Dr. Mrs. Claudiana Ibijoke and Wife of the Deputy Governor of Lagos State, Mrs. Oluremi Hamzat, during the Monthly Environmental Sanitation Exercise, held on the 25th of July, 2026, at Ibeju-Lekki Local Government, Lagos State[/caption] [caption id="attachment_7359" align="alignleft" width="1022"] From left: Chairman, Badagry Local Government, Hon. Babatunde Hunpe; Special Adviser on Environment, Engr. Olakunle Rotimi-Akodu, right, Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Dr. Gaji Omobolaji, during the Monthly Environmental Sanitation Exercise, held on 25th of July, 2026,at Badagry Local Government, Lagos State.[/caption] [caption id="attachment_7358" align="alignleft" width="932"] L-R: Chairman, Badagry Local Government, Hon. Babatunde Hunpe, APC Deputy Governor Gubernatorial Candidate in Lagos state, Princess. Damilola Sonayan James and Special Adviser on Environment, Engr.Olakunle Rotimi-Akodu, engaged in cleaning during the Monthly Environmental Sanitation Exercise, held in Badagry Local Government on Saturday the 25th of July, 2026.[/caption] [caption id="attachment_7357" align="alignleft" width="2400"] L-R: Honourable Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab; Ologunfayo of Ogunfayo Kingdom, Ibeju-Lekki, HRM Oba. Dr. Mufutau Olanrewaju Idogun (Tunwase 1); Wife of the Deputy Governor of Lagos State, Mrs. Oluremi Hamzat and First Lady of Lagos State, Dr. (Mrs) Claudiana Ibijoke Sanwo-Olu, during the Monthly Environmental Sanitation Exercise, held on the 25th of July, 2026, at Ibeju-Lekki Local Government, Lagos State[/caption]
Also speaking, Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Tokunbo Wahab informed that work is at an advanced stage at Olusosun and Simpson with respect to the Transfer Loading Stations that are being constructed there.
 "The ultimate goal is, once they are completed, there'll be a material recovery facility at Ikorodu and Badagry to cart away the waste. And we believe we are going to get there
And I believe LAWMA and the PSP operators are also putting in a lot of effort. We just have to keep doing the advocacy and appealing to our people to manage the waste properly. People should take ownership rather than just pick up their waste and dump it on the median and all", Wahab explained.
He affirmed that the State is gaining traction in the battle again filth and indiscriminate waste dumping but that some habits that are built over time also take a while to change, adding that consistency, advocacy and proper messaging will take us there.
He appealed to residents not to dump waste indiscriminately to people but rather call the attention of LAWMA through its Toll Free lines if a particular PSP operator is not coming to pick waste so that  LAWMA can intervene in the interim.
 Meanwhile, in Badagry Local Government, where the Special Adviser on the Environment, Engr Kunle Rotimi-Akodu led other officials, including Permanent Secretaries, to monitor, he reiterated the unwavering commitment of the State to sustaining a cleaner, healthier and more resilient environment.
Akodu commended the people of Badagry for embracing environmental sanitation as a civic responsibility, noting that the level of compliance recorded during the exercise was encouraging.
According to him, the Lagos State Government is driving a behavioural change campaign aimed at transforming waste management practices across the State through sustained public enlightenment and community engagement.
"The culture we seek to build is one where every resident takes responsibility for the environment; Poor waste disposal habits contribute significantly to environmental degradation and flooding; We must all embrace proper waste management practices to safeguard our communities," he said.
Responding to concerns raised by the council over the shortage of Private Sector Participation (PSP) waste operators servicing parts of Badagry, the Special Adviser assured residents that the Ministry would immediately review the complaint and work with the relevant regulatory authorities to address any identified service gaps.
Earlier, the Chairman of Badagry Local Government, Mr Babatunde Hunpe, expressed appreciation to the Governor for his unwavering support for environmental sustainability and thanked the Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources for bringing the monitoring exercise to the area.
The Chairman disclosed that the council has continued to complement the operations of PSP operators through its intervention teams and waste evacuation trucks while carrying out sustained environmental advocacy across markets, communities, Community Development Associations (CDAs) and other grassroots platforms.
The APC Gubernatorial Candidate, Princess Damilola Sonayan-James, who also participated during the clean-up, urged all residents to sustain the momentum by continually cleaning up their environment and patronising assigned PSP operators.
She further said residents should avoid indiscriminate waste disposal and ensure drains, roadsides and public spaces remain free of refuse, stressing that environmental sustainability can only be achieved through collective responsibility and consistent compliance with environmental laws.
The monitoring exercise, which covered Ajara Market and adjoining communities, witnessed impressive participation from residents, traders, Community Development Committees (CDCs), youth organisations, students and other stakeholders, reflecting a growing commitment to environmental stewardship across the council area.
Also present at the clean-up were the Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Dr Gaji Omobolaji, Permanent Secretary Office of Drainage Services, Engr Mahamood Adegbite, some Heads of Agencies as well as Directors in the Ministry.

item.title: LASG SEEKS, GETS COMMUNITIES BUY-IN TO COMMENCE WORK ON MATERIAL RECOVERY FACILITY (MRF) AT AGBOWA
item.dc:creator: moel
item.content:encoded:
The Lagos State Government on Monday engaged the traditional rulers and leaders of the Owu Ikosi and Agbowa Ikosi communities on the need to collaborate and ensure the early commencement of work on a proposed Material Recovery Facility (MRF) in Agbowa in the Epe division.
This is just as the traditional rulers, the Abowa of Agbowa Ikosi, Oba Owolabi Momson and the Olowu of Owu Ikosi, Oba Nelson Ogunlari gave a commitment on behalf of their communities for the State government to commence work on the proposed project right away.
Speaking during a meeting with the traditional rulers and chiefs of the two communities, Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab, stressed the need for broad-based community acceptance and ownership of the project by the two communities to prevent any form of disagreement.
Wahab explained that the proposed MRF should be viewed as a major development initiative rather than merely a waste recovery facility, noting that the Lagos State Government had been deliberate in spreading critical infrastructure and development projects across the State.
The Commissioner noted that the meeting was convened to resolve outstanding concerns and ensure that all parties were adequately carried along before the State proceeds with the project.
[caption id="attachment_7366" align="alignleft" width="1280"] L-R: Permanent Secretary, Lands Bureau, Mr Kamar Olowosago, Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Dr Gaji Omobolaji, Honorable Commissioner, for the Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab, Director from the Surveyor General's Office, Surv O. Ogunbiyi, Acting Surveyor General, Mr Odupe Olalekan, Managing Director LAWMA, Dr Muyiwa Gbadegesin during a stakeholders meeting held in Ministry of the Environment Conference room on the 24Th of August, 2026.[/caption]
 
According to him, while the State has a mandate to deliver sustainable waste management infrastructure, it is equally committed to ensuring that communities hosting such projects understand, accept and ultimately take ownership of them.
“It is a major development we are bringing to that site, and we have been very deliberate about how we spread development across the State; this meeting is to resolve whatever the issues are. We have to be frank because we do not want to make any mistake,” he said.
[caption id="attachment_7365" align="alignleft" width="1080"] The Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Dr Gaji Omobolaji, Permanent Secretary, Lands Bureau, Mr Kamar Olowoshago, Abowa of Agbowa Ikosi, Oba Saheed Momson, Honourable Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab, Olowu of Owu Ikosi, Oba Nelson Ogunlari, Executive Director Finance LAWMA, Mr Kunle Adebiyi, Permanent Secretary, Office of Drainage Service and Water Resources, Engr. Mahamood Adegbite, Ag. Surveyor General, Mr Odupe Olalekan, Director from the Surveyor General's Office, Surv. O. Ogunbiyi, and the Managing Director LAWMA, Dr Muyiwa Gbadegesin during a stakeholders meeting held in Ministry of the Environment Conference room on the 24th of August, 2026.[/caption]
The Commissioner subsequently reaffirmed the State Government’s commitment to ensuring that both communities are fully carried along, with the traditional institutions and relevant government agencies working together to resolve any issues that may arise in the course of the project.
He stressed that no side would be favoured at the expense of the other, adding that the objective was to achieve an arrangement that would promote development while respecting the interests of the two communities.
Wahab, acknowledging the role of the two traditional rulers, the Abowa of Agbowa-Ikosi, Oba Saheed Momson, and the Olowu of Owu-Ikosi, Oba Nelson Ogunlari, in helping to resolve the concerns, noted that their willingness to see the “bigger picture” and prioritise the development of the area was very commendable.
Wahab further assured the stakeholders that the concerns raised by the traditional institutions and community representatives would be given due consideration, stressing that the State Government would not impose the project without carrying the affected communities along.
The Commissioner said the State Government would ensure that the agreed positions from the meeting were formally documented through correspondence to all stakeholders, providing a clear framework for subsequent actions.
He assured the stakeholders that the Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources, the Lagos State Waste Management Authority (LAWMA), the Ministry of Physical Planning and Urban Development, the Lands Bureau, the consultants and other relevant agencies would continue to work together to achieve success on the project.
Also speaking, the Permanent Secretary, Lands Bureau, Mr. Kamar Olowoshago, expressed appreciation to the traditional rulers, chiefs, community leaders and other stakeholders for their constructive engagement, saying it is to his delight that work can now commence on the Agbowa, Epe location just as it has started in the Erekiti location in Badagry.
The Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Dr Gaji Omobolaji, stated that the proposed Material Recovery Facility is expected to strengthen waste recovery, recycling and resource utilisation while supporting the State Government’s efforts to reduce the volume of waste ultimately disposed of at landfills.
He reiterated that the administration of Governor Babajide Olusola Sanwo-Olu remained committed to implementing sustainable environmental solutions across Lagos, while ensuring that communities are active partners in projects that directly affect them.
Responding jointly, the Olowu of Owu-Ikosi, Oba Nelson Ogunlari and  the Abowa of Agbowa- Ikosi, Oba Owolabi Momson jointly   expressed their support for development initiative that would improve the communities, while urging the State Government to ensure that all relevant stakeholders are properly consulted and carried along.
They explained that the communities were not opposed to development, saying the presentation of the project and its proposed facilities was satisfactory.
 He added that the state government must ensure that all components contained in the project plan are fully implemented.
Also present at the meeting were Permanent Secretary, Office of Drainage Services, Engr. Mahamood Adegbite; and the Acting Surveyor-General of Lagos State, Surv. Olalekan Odupe.
Others included the Managing Director of LAWMA, Dr. Muyiwa Gbadegesin; Executive Director, Finance, LAWMA, Mr. Kunle Adebiyi; as well as other top officials in the Ministry.
Signed
Kunle Adeshina
Director Public Affairs
MOE&WR
24th August, 2026

item.title: LAGOS SEEKS STRONGER REGULATION, COLLABORATION WITH WASTE MANAGERS TO IMPROVE WASTE DISPOSAL
item.dc:creator: moel
item.content:encoded:
The Lagos State Government has reiterated its commitment to strengthening the regulation of Private Sector Participation (PSP) operators and improving waste collection, transportation and disposal across the State.

The Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab, stated this on Wednesday during a meeting with the executive members of the Association of Waste Managers of Nigeria (AWAMN), held as part of ongoing efforts to address operational challenges affecting the State’s waste management system.

The meeting provided an opportunity for the Government and waste management operators to review developments across the waste management value chain, with particular attention to the condition of dumpsites, challenges confronting PSP operators and measures required to improve operational efficiency and reduce turnaround time for waste collection and disposal.

[caption id="attachment_7370" align="alignleft" width="1280"] (1). L-R. The Secretary General of the Association of Waste Managers of Nigeria (AWAMN) Mr Taiye Kolade, The President of the Association Waste Managers of Nigeria ( AWAMN) Dr Olugbega Adebola, and the Honourable Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab, during a stakeholder meeting with Executive Members of the Association of Waste Managers of Nigeria held in Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources conference room on the 27th of August, 2026.[/caption]

Wahab stressed the need for all stakeholders in the sector to work towards a common objective of establishing an effective, efficient and sustainable waste management system in Lagos. He noted that the Government would continue to engage operators to identify challenges and develop practical solutions.

While acknowledging recent improvements at landfill sites across the State, the Commissioner emphasised the need for further interventions to make the facilities fully functional, efficient and sustainable.

[caption id="attachment_7369" align="alignleft" width="1280"] The Honourable Commissioner for the Environment and water Resource Mr Tokunbo Wahab, The Permanent Secretary Office of the Drainage Service and water Resources Engr. Mahamood Adegbite, Executive Director LAWMA, Mr Kunle Adebiyi, during a stakeholder meeting with the Executive Members of the Association of Waste Managers of Nigeria held in Ministry of the Environment and water Resources Conference room on the 27th of August, 2026.[/caption]

He also reiterated the importance of providing proper access roads, drainage systems, operational platforms and other essential facilities to facilitate the smooth movement of waste trucks within the dumpsites.

According to him, ongoing improvements at the Solous dumpsite would significantly reduce pressure on other disposal locations, particularly those serving Alimosho, Ikotun-Ejigbo, Ayobo and surrounding communities. He added that the improvements would also reduce turnaround time for PSP operators and enable them to provide more efficient services to residents.

The Commissioner further disclosed that the State Government was exploring measures to improve the financial sustainability of PSP operations, including cost recovery mechanisms and appropriate adjustments that would enable operators to deliver their services more effectively.

He, however, stressed that improved financial arrangements must be matched by accountability, transparency and effective service delivery.

“No PSP operator should use the challenges at the dumpsites or other operational difficulties as an excuse for failing to provide the required services to residents,” he said.

Wahab called on AWAMN to strengthen its internal regulatory mechanisms and ensure that every PSP operator fulfils its contractual obligations, maintains its fleet and provides consistent waste collection services within its assigned areas.

He also expressed support for the association’s proposal to have environmental officers attached to wards across the State to monitor waste management activities at the community level.

He explained that the officers would help ensure that household waste is properly collected, payments for waste services are made, PSP operators perform efficiently and residents receive continuous sensitisation on proper waste disposal practices.

Wahab also stressed that effective enforcement would be critical to ensuring that residents patronise designated PSP operators and desist from indiscriminate disposal of waste on roads and other unauthorised locations.

He urged AWAMN to submit its recommendations on sustainable waste management for further consideration by the State Government. The proposals are expected to cover enforcement, cost recovery, waste treatment and disposal, as well as the regulation of PSP operators.

AWAMN Commends Lagos Government

Responding, the President of AWAMN, Dr. Olugbenga Adebola, commended the Ministry and its leadership for their commitment and personal intervention in addressing challenges within the waste management sector.

Adebola said the association had responded to the Government’s directives by inspecting disposal sites and engaging contractors to undertake improvement works at some dumpsite locations.

He disclosed that the association had also worked with officials of the Lagos State Waste Management Authority (LAWMA) to identify infrastructure and operational requirements at the various dumpsites.

According to him, some access roads had been opened and improved, while further work, including stone-base reinforcement, was required to ensure that the roads remain functional during the rainy season and can withstand the weight of heavy waste trucks.

The AWAMN President also called for increased attention to the management and maintenance of disposal facilities, noting that adequate operational platforms and equipment were essential to improving turnaround time and preventing unnecessary delays for waste trucks.

Adebola further disclosed that the association had established a dumpsite committee to work with relevant government agencies in monitoring activities at disposal facilities and developing solutions to identified operational challenges.

On PSP operations, Adebola said the association was ready to collaborate with the State Government in developing a comprehensive and sustainable waste management framework that would go beyond waste collection and transportation to encompass disposal, waste treatment, enforcement and cost recovery.

Present at the meeting were the Permanent Secretary, Office of Drainage Services, Engr. Mahamood Adegbite; Executive Director, Finance, LAWMA, Mr. Kunle Adebiyi; and Directors in the Ministry.

Signed

Adekunle Adeshina Director, Public Affairs Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources

27 August 2026

item.title: LAGOS TO GET OVER 200 NEW COMPACTOR TRUCKS TO IMPROVE WASTE EVACUATION
item.dc:creator: moel
item.content:encoded:
....As Deputy Governor Kadri Hamzat leads wife, Oluremi, HOS, HC Env, SA Env. other officials to monitor sanitation in Festac & Bariga

The Lagos State Government is set to take delivery of over 200 new compactor trucks as part of measures to strengthen waste collection and evacuation across the State.

The Deputy Governor of Lagos State, Dr. Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, disclosed this on Saturday while leading his wife, Oluremi Hamzat, and other top government officials to monitor the August monthly environmental sanitation exercise in the Amuwo-Odofin Local Government Area.

Speaking to journalists in Festac Town after participating in the cleaning exercise, Hamzat urged residents to desist from patronising unregistered cart pushers and instead ensure that their waste is handed over to registered Private Sector Participation (PSP) waste operators.

He said residents have an important role to play in ensuring that waste does not end up in unauthorised locations, particularly drainage channels and canals, which could contribute to flooding.

“What we need our people to also do is to make sure that they patronise their PSP, not the cart pushers. Because those ones are not organised. You don't know where it is ending up. But the PSP will take it to the landfills. The cart pushers, we don't know. It might even be in the canals.”

Hamzat added that residents' cooperation was essential to preventing indiscriminate waste disposal and protecting the environment.

“That's the encouragement that we're giving our citizens—to make sure that you play your role and ensure that the garbage doesn't end up in a canal and therefore lead to flooding,” he said.

The Deputy Governor described the monthly environmental sanitation exercise as an important initiative aimed at promoting a culture of environmental responsibility among residents.

According to him, maintaining a healthy environment requires the collective participation of government and citizens.

“We cannot be a people without a healthy environment,” he said.

[caption id="attachment_7377" align="alignleft" width="1536"] Deputy Governor of Lagos State, Dr. Obafemi Hamzat, (third right), Honourable Commissioner for The Environment and Water Resources, Mr.Tokunbo Wahab (Second right) with them are staff of Amuwo Odofin Local Government and School Pupils, during the August Monthly Environmental Sanitation Exercise, held on the 29th of August, 2026, at Amuwo Odofin Local Government, Lagos State.[/caption] [caption id="attachment_7376" align="alignleft" width="1536"] L-R: Deputy Governor of Lagos State, Dr. Obafemi Hamzat: Chairman, Amuwo Odofin Local Government, Prince Lanre Sanusi and Honourable Commissioner for The Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab,
during the August Monthly Environmental Sanitation Exercise, held on the 29th of August, 2026, at Amuwo Odofin Local Government, Lagos State.[/caption] [caption id="attachment_7375" align="alignleft" width="1264"] From left: Wife of the Deputy Governor of Lagos State, Mrs. Oluremi Hamzat: Honourable Commissioner for The Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab: Deputy Governor of Lagos State, Dr. Obafemi Hamzat and the Special Adviser on Environment, Engr. Olakunle Rotimi-Akodu (right), during the August Monthly Environmental Sanitation Exercise, held on the 29th of August, 2026, at Amuwo Odofin Local Government, Lagos State.[/caption] [caption id="attachment_7374" align="alignleft" width="1264"] L:R : Special Adviser on Environment, Engr. Olakunle Rotimi-Akodu; Deputy Governor of Lagos State, Dr. Obafemi Hamzat and Honourable Commissioner for The Environment and Water Resources, Mr.Tokunbo Wahab, during the Monthly Environmental Sanitation Exercise, held on the 29th of August, 2026, at Amuwo Odofin Local Government, Lagos State.[/caption]

Government Intensifies Efforts to Address Waste on Medians

Also speaking during the exercise on measures to address the accumulation of waste on road medians, the Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Mr. Tokunbo Wahab, who was accompanied by the Special Adviser on the Environment, Engr. Kunle Rotimi-Akodu, said the situation was gradually improving.

Wahab disclosed that the Ministry had established emergency response teams operating 24 hours daily to address environmental challenges, while efforts were also ongoing to improve landfill and dumpsite infrastructure across the State.

He said the Ministry would continue to engage PSP waste operators while intervening where necessary to improve their operational capacity and service delivery.

The Commissioner expressed optimism that improved waste collection services would encourage more residents to pay their waste bills, thereby strengthening the financial sustainability of PSP operations.

On measures to curb the activities of cart pushers, Wahab said the Government was engaging with them but stressed that any solution adopted must take into consideration the long-term environmental and security implications.

He said:

“We don't want to say because we're in a situation, we take steps that will come to harm us later in life. Most of these cart pushers, ask yourself, where is the waste usually dumped? Drainage, medians and so on.”

The Commissioner further noted that security findings had raised concerns about the involvement of some cart pushers in other criminal activities.

“In addition to that, security findings have also shown that some of them are part of those gangs involved in cutting metals and doing all sorts. We can't go that route,” Wahab reiterated.

HOS Urges Residents to Make Cleanliness an Everyday Responsibility

Meanwhile, the Head of Service, Mr. Olabode Agoro, who led another team of government officials to Bariga LCDA to monitor the exercise, urged residents to take greater responsibility for the cleanliness of their surroundings.

He also warned that individuals and establishments found violating environmental laws would face appropriate sanctions.

Agoro, who was represented by the Permanent Secretary, Public Service Office, Mrs. Sunkanmi Oyegbola, stressed that government alone could not achieve a cleaner and healthier Lagos without the active participation and cooperation of residents.

He said government officials were participating in the sanitation exercise to lead by example and encourage residents to embrace environmental cleanliness as a collective responsibility.

The Head of Service urged residents not to wait until the last Saturday of the month before cleaning their surroundings, but to make environmental cleanliness an everyday practice.

“We are here to ensure that the environment is clean and to encourage citizens to come out and clean their surroundings. Government has declared this day for residents to participate in environmental sanitation, and we are here to lead by example and encourage everyone to join us,” he said.

Prominent among government officials who participated in the monitoring exercise across the locations were the Commissioner for Special Duties and Intergovernmental Relations, Mr. Gbenga Oyerinde; Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Mr. Gaji Omobolaji Tajudeen; Permanent Secretary, Office of Drainage Services, Engr. Olakunle Adegbite; other Permanent Secretaries; Local Government Chairmen; heads of government agencies; and members of the Committee of Wives of Lagos State Officials (COWLSO).

Signed
